name: פַּגְעִיאֵל
gloss: meeting of God; or entreaty of God
summary: The son of Ochran, prince of Asher in the wilderness: he stood with Moses and Aaron at the numbering, camped as Asher's prince beside Dan on the north, brought Asher's offering on the eleventh day of the altar's dedication, and led Asher's host when the camps set out from Sinai (Num 1:13; 2:27; 7:72; 10:26). The name joins the noun פֶּגַע of the root פגע, “meet”, with the linking ־ִי, to אֵל, God: “God's meeting”, one whom God has met. Since the root also means to entreat and intercede (Jer 7:16; Isa 53:12), “entreaty of God” is possible too; no verse says why he was so named.

evidence.note: “Over the host of the tribe of the sons of Asher, פַּגְעִיאֵל son of Ochran.”
“For Asher, Pagiel son of Ochran”, among the men who stood with Moses and Aaron.
The prince of the sons of Asher, camped beside Dan.
On the eleventh day, Pagiel brings Asher's offering (to 7:77).
“This was the offering of Pagiel son of Ochran.”
The root's verb with God's side as the one meeting: “the messengers of God met (וַיִּפְגְּעוּ) him”.
“You meet (פָּגַעְתָּ) him who rejoices and works righteousness”: God meeting a man.
The verb of entreating God, for the second reading.

note: BDB key q.ag.ad (Num 1:13; 2:27; 7:72, 77; 10:26). The first element is read as the noun פֶּגַע (1Ki 5:18; Ecc 9:11) with the linking ־ִי found in other names in ־ִיאֵל; it could also be the verb with a pronoun. Whether God is the one who meets or the one entreated the name alone does not show.
